title: API unit econ regional scenario grid and quick experiments
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic workbook (sheet-style) to drive 6-week experiments that reduce per-token hosted COGS and validate margin improvement levers by model family and region. Intended as a cross-functional handoff doc for Product-Optimize + Serving-Runtime + Pricing. Not final — live scratchpad with sensitivity grid, assumptions, and prioritized experiments.

High-level summary (one-liner):
Target 12–20% improvement in per-token gross margin for mid/high-latency chat workloads by combining smarter batching, lightweight KV-prefix caching, and one targeted quantization profile per model family.

Assumptions (kept explicit so numbers are reproducible):
- Billing price baseline: US region default price = $0.015 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.03 per 1k completion tokens (example blended starting point for mid-sized model families).
- Current observed COGS baseline (hosted infra + amortized infra ops):
  - Redwood-alpha-1 (large): $0.0048 per 1k tokens
  - Open-7b: $0.0019 per 1k tokens
  - Falcon-40b: $0.0065 per 1k tokens
- Latency buckets used for SLO segmentation: low (<100ms), mid (100–350ms), high (>350ms). Most interactive chat traffic sits in mid bucket today.
- Regional infra multiplier (cost to serve relative to US baseline): US=1.00, EU=1.12, APAC=1.28. (Includes cloud instance uplift + network).
- Typical request composition: 35% prompts-only (embeddings/short), 65% prompts+completions. Average completion length = 64 tokens.

Sensitivity grid (compact CSV lines to paste into sheet):
columns: model_family,region,baseline_cogs_per_1k,price_per_1k,baseline_margin_pct,scenario,delta_cogs_pct,scenario_cogs_per_1k,scenario_margin_pct,notes
rows:
redwood-alpha-1,US,0.0048,0.015,68,aggressive-batching,-18,0.00394,74,enable continuous batching + reduce idle micro-batches
redwood-alpha-1,EU,0.00538,0.015,64,kv-cache-light,-12,0.00422,72,prefix cache for common system prompts (TTL 60s)
redwood-alpha-1,APAC,0.00614,0.015,59,quant-8bit,-22,0.00374,75,validated quant profile 8-bit dynamic for chat sequences
open-7b,US,0.0019,0.006,68,micro-ops-batch,-25,0.00143,76,aggressive batching for small context windows
open-7b,EU,0.00213,0.006,64,cache-only,-10,0.00192,68,cache prompt prefixes for intent routing
falcon-40b,US,0.0065,0.02,67,hybrid-quant-batching,-20,0.0052,74,mixed strategy: int8 + batching

Key formulas to reproduce in sheet (explicit text so engineers can port):
- baseline_margin_pct = (price_per_1k - baseline_cogs_per_1k) / price_per_1k * 100
- scenario_cogs_per_1k = baseline_cogs_per_1k * (1 - delta_cogs_pct/100)
- scenario_margin_pct = (price_per_1k - scenario_cogs_per_1k) / price_per_1k * 100

Operational levers (short descriptions + quick win estimate):
1) Continuous micro-batching tuning (RW-runtime): aim for 15–25% lower per-token GPU time for mid-latency workload; risk: tail-latency regressions for very short prompts. Quick win estimate: 10–20% cost reduction on models with <1k context.
2) KV prefix caching for common assistant/system prompts (Console + routing): reduces repeated compute for identical prefix tokens. Expect 8–15% for high-reuse traffic segments.
3) One production quant profile per model family (8-bit + per-layer calibration): saves 18–25% on per-token GPU cost but requires validation (quality A/B).
4) Region-aware routing policy: route latency-tolerant requests to cheaper region replicas during normal load and failover. Saves up to 8% on blended token COGS; requires network and compliance gating.
5) Bump OS scheduling + host recovery heuristics (SRE): reduce small tail wastes (idle slots) — 3–6% improvement.

Prioritized experiments (6-week plan):
- Week 0–2: Micro-batching configuration sweep (owners: Samir + runtime). Measure tokens/sec and p50/p95 latencies across model families. Deliverable: A/B experiment template + traffic segment analysis.
- Week 2–4: KV prefix cache prototype for top-10 prompt templates (owners: Evelyn + console). Measure cache hit rate and end-to-end latency change; define eviction TTL.
- Week 3–5: Quantization smoke test on canary cluster (owner: Jonah + applied-ml). Small percent of traffic diverted to quantized variant with automated evals on production-style prompts.
- Week 5–6: Regional routing alpha: route shopper intent class to EU/APAC cheaper replicas during off-peak; monitor error rate & SLO. (owner: Maya + platform-eng).

Quick scenario note: break-even pricing sensitivity
- If blended COGS for redwood-alpha-1 (US) moves to 0.0039 per 1k tokens (aggressive improvements), the minimal price to preserve current margin (baseline margin ~68%) can be reduced ~8% without losing gross margin dollars. This is useful when designing promotional pricing for high-usage customers.

Example charts to add to sheet (descriptions):
- Heatmap: delta-margin (%) across model family vs region (cells colored by scenario_margin_pct change).
- Waterfall: baseline price -> baseline COGS -> post-lever COGS -> scenario margin -> implied price headroom.
- Hit-rate vs cost reduction plot for KV cache (x=hit rate, y=%cogs saved).

Open questions / risks (tracked):
- Quality drift risk with 8-bit quant across low-resource languages (need eval set coverage per-region).
- Operational complexity of region-aware routing for multi-tenant customers with data-residency constraints.
- Impact on observability cost (tracing+metrics) when enabling aggressive batching — ensure sampling policy adjusted.

Acceptance criteria for experiment success (per-experiment):
- Micro-batching: >=10% end-to-end per-token cost reduction on test traffic while p95 latency increase <=10% absolute and error rate delta <0.05%.
- KV-cache: >=6% blended COGS reduction for the routed traffic segment with cache hit >=18% and negligible correctness regressions.
- Quantization: quality delta (LLM eval score) <=1% on primary evals; COGS reduction >=15%.

Back-of-envelope impact if all prioritized experiments succeed (company-level blended assumption):
- Blended hosted COGS down 16% -> gross margin on hosted API improves ~6–9 percentage points depending on price elasticity. Rough revenue-neutral promotion opportunity: lower price up to ~7% while maintaining gross contribution.

Action items (concrete next steps, assign and date):
- Samir: kick off continuous batching sweep, create measurement harness (due 2025-01-20).
- Evelyn: prototype KV prefix cache and add feature flag in console routing (due 2025-01-28).
- Jonah: finalize quantization calibration script and small canary (due 2025-02-04).
- Maya: draft pricing headroom brief and coordinate legal for regional routing constraints (due 2025-02-11).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact and slightly messy — paste the CSV rows into the working sheet tab named "scenario-grid"; expand rows into full tables and add the waterfall and heatmap. Flag any missing traffic segments we should model (e.g., long-context fine-tuning generation jobs).

- Current regional rate card snapshot (internal sheet): https://sheets.redwood/company/hosted-ratecard-2025q1
